S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

symptom.disease_info: Schizophrenia is a chronic psychotic disorder characterized by disturbances in thought, perception, and behavior, including delusions, hallucinations, disorganized thinking, and negative symptoms such as diminished motivation and emotional expression. Onset typically occurs in late adolescence or early adulthood, but later-life onset and relapses can occur, with a course that ranges from episodic to progressively deteriorating. Functional impairment in work, relationships, and self-care is common, often persisting beyond acute episodes if negative symptoms or cognitive deficits are prominent. It is differentiated from mood and substance-induced psychotic disorders by the relative independence of psychotic symptoms from mood episodes and the absence of a direct physiological cause.

patient.stressor: Around two years ago, Brent was in the middle of expanding his boutique financial advisory practice when he went through a tumultuous breakup with a long-term partner who had been deeply involved in his social and arts circles. In the months that followed, he threw himself into work and the Cincinnati arts scene, but colleagues and family noticed he became increasingly preoccupied with certain clients and local art patrons, interpreting minor business setbacks and awkward social interactions as part of a broader pattern of people working against him. Over time this preoccupation began to erode his easy rapport with clients; he canceled meetings at the last minute, dropped out of his usual pick-up basketball games, and cut short trips he had meticulously planned, saying he didn’t feel safe or welcome. His sister ultimately pushed him to see a psychiatrist after he confided to her that he was convinced specific people in his professional and art networks were secretly coordinating to undermine his reputation and practice, despite repeated reassurances and lack of concrete evidence.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’m convinced certain people in my professional and art circles are secretly working together to damage my reputation and my practice, even though everyone keeps telling me it’s not really happening.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: It’s gotten to the point where, when a client suddenly reschedules or an art patron doesn’t return an email, I’m sure it’s because there’s this quiet group chat or email chain where they’re coordinating how to freeze me out and ruin my name, and no amount of people telling me I’m overthinking it really shakes that feeling anymore.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: Most days now I just sit in my apartment after work with the TV on mute, ignoring texts and calls, because I can’t seem to make myself care about going to gallery openings, meeting friends, or even cooking a real meal, and when I do drag myself out I feel flat and disconnected, like I’m just going through the motions for other people’s sake.
